objective: Add an executable source-subset normalization and QC contract, fail-closed temporal controls, and deterministic materialization without weakening scientific validation semantics.

baseline.description: Source-backed validation requires explicit provenance, normalization, QC, temporal controls, and deterministic evidence materialization; immutable benchmark truth remains separate from mutable live-source evidence.

correctness.reason: This change establishes executable contracts and regression coverage; no scientific accuracy delta is claimed.

reliability.reason: Operational reliability is protected by deterministic normalization, QC, and fail-closed temporal controls; no production reliability delta is claimed.

reproducibility.reason: The change improves reproducibility controls but does not yet establish immutable external-source reproduction.

coverage.reason: Source-subset coverage is contractually checked; this PR does not claim completion of the full external benchmark set.

measurement.trade_off: Large source datasets remain external; only normalized evidence and manifests are materialized. Live-source data is never promoted to immutable benchmark truth.

evidence: Source-subset normalization and QC are executable and regression-tested.
Temporal cutoff enforcement is fail-closed and deterministic.
Materialization is deterministic and keeps large source data outside Git.
The permanent scientific gate remains fail-closed; this PR does not weaken benchmark thresholds or resolve the independent historical ALeRCE drift blocker.

findings: Source-backed validation requires normalization and QC contracts before evidence can be consumed reproducibly.
Temporal controls must fail closed when a source subset cannot establish the required cutoff.
Deterministic evidence materialization should version manifests and derived evidence, not large external datasets.
